newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakura warns of foreign investment currency risk.
newsitem.headline: Sakura warns of foreign investment currency risk.

text.p: Japanese retail investors need to be more aware of currency risks posed by mushrooming purchases of bonds and securities denominated in foreign currencies, Sakura Institute of Research said on Tuesday.

It estimated in a report that Japanese investors bought a total of about 10 trillion yen worth of foreign bonds and stocks in 1996 as they sought higher returns amid ultra-low domestic interest rates.
Sakura estimated the value of foreign bonds and securities held by Japanese investors to have reached a record high of about 100 trillion yen by the end of 1996.
It said foreign asset holdings were boosted due to an assumption by investors that the yen would not appreciate sharply in the longer term.
Investors estimated there was little chance of the yen appreciating above 105 yen to the dollar in the next year.
In the longer term, investors were not expecting the yen to appreciate above 95 yen in five years or above 90 yen in 10 years, it said.

Sakura also said there was a possibility of a revival of the yen's uptrend, which could be triggered by the ending of the current ultra-low domestic interest rate policy or a possible rise in Japan's trade surplus.
Given such factors, the currency risks involved in foreign financial asset investment could grow if the yen actually started to appreciate rapidly.
